concept.name: Average true range
concept.definition: Welles Wilder's volatility measure (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978): the Wilder-smoothed average of True Range, where True Range is the greatest of the current high-low span, |high - prior close|, and |low - prior close| - capturing gap and limit-move volatility that a plain high-low range misses.
concept.intuition: ATR tells you how much an instrument typically moves per bar, with no directional content: it expands in violent markets and contracts in quiet ones.
concept.mechanics: TR_t = max(High - Low, |High - Close_prev|, |Low - Close_prev|). The first 14-period ATR is the SMA of the first 14 TR values; thereafter ATR_t = (ATR_{t-1} x 13 + TR_t) / 14. Used for stop distances, position sizing, and breakout validation.
concept.failure_modes: ATR is in absolute price units, so values are not comparable across securities or across large price changes in one security; the recursive Wilder smoothing makes early values seed-dependent and needs long histories (StockCharts calculates back 250+ periods) to stabilize.
concept.misconceptions: ATR says nothing about direction - a falling ATR during a rally is not bearish, just quietening; and a high ATR is not by itself a top signal.
concept.example: StockCharts' spreadsheet: the first 14-day ATR comes out at 0.56, and ATR surged as QQQ plunged with long candlesticks in May.
